leaf_reflect_nir.reason: held at the PFT file's value with the albedo target off (owner, 2026-10-04): at realistic leaf optics the model's canopy reflects too much NIR, and the albedo pushed the leaf's reflectance to 0.32 (prior z -3.1; reflectance + transmittance 0.57 against ~0.70 for tropical leaves) to make up for it. Revisit with the canopy's structure (clumping, wood optics)

leaf_transmit_nir.reason: the albedo sees the leaf's NIR reflectance and transmittance only as their sum: fit one of the two

leaf_reflect_vis.reason: a tower barely sees the visible optics: the leaf absorbs most of the PAR at any value in the range

leaf_transmit_vis.reason: a tower barely sees the visible optics: the leaf absorbs most of the PAR at any value in the range

leaf_clumping.reason: held at the base value (0.80: ED2's tropical trees and lianas; FATES uses 0.85 for broadleaf evergreen tropical trees): the albedo cannot tell it from the leaf NIR reflectance (Jacobian correlation 0.986), and the fits sent it to either bound with the energy targets' treatment (owner, 2026-10-02)

theta_j.reason: held at the PFT file's value (0.7 in the reference PFTs: the effective curvature of a mean-light cohort). A tower cannot tell it from the canopy's light distribution or from the error in its respiration; fit 3 drove it to its floor to absorb the GPP offset. Revisit with sunlit/shaded leaves (see docs/ROADMAP.md)

jmax_vcmax_ratio.reason: fixed at Kattge & Knorr (2007) for the site's growth temperature (2.59 - 0.035 T), computed from the forcing; a shape key, never fitted beside kappa (best-practice plan §3.5, §4.3)

phi_psii.reason: the electron yield of linear transport in low light (0.74: 0.37 electrons per absorbed photon, the measured maximum CO2 yield 0.093 of Long et al. 1993 at 4 electrons per CO2). A tower's dim-light GPP cannot tell it from the error in the tower's respiration, so the leaf measurements set it

ds_vcmax.reason: fixed at Kattge & Knorr (2007) for the site's growth temperature (668.39 - 1.07 T), computed from the forcing (best-practice plan §3.5)

ds_jmax.reason: fixed at Kattge & Knorr (2007) for the site's growth temperature (659.70 - 0.75 T), computed from the forcing (best-practice plan §3.5)

d_ratio.reason: it moves the fluxes as z0m_ratio does: fit one of the two

leaf_width.reason: it sets only the leaves' boundary-layer conductance, which a tower's fluxes barely inform

dsl_dmax.reason: it sets only soil evaporation, a small part of LE under a closed canopy

leaf_surf_water_max.reason: the tower does not see the wet canopy: at BCI FLAG gap-fills every raining hour and 56 % of the three hours after (an open-path analyser's usual loss), so a fit tunes it on dry hours only (owner, 2026-10-02). A tower that measures through rain may fit it

wood_surf_water_max.reason: as leaf_surf_water_max; the tower cannot tell the wood film from the leaf film

intercept_k.reason: it acts only through the wet canopy, which a tower that gap-fills its rain hours never samples, and its response can be rough

stomata_psi_onset.reason: held at half the PFT's turgor-loss point (owner, 2026-10-04): the BCI fit took it to its bound (-0.16 MPa, prior z +2.6), set by the ten-day windows' upwelling longwave and LE rather than the drought runs (test T6), and traded it against stomatal_g1 (correlation 0.91). wstress_sref_stomata carries the drought response

rd_vcmax_ratio.reason: night NEE leaves the fast fit (owner, 2026-10-02); the target that informed it pulled it to its floor

leaf_angle_mean.prior_source: the PFT file's value, +-10 degrees; spherical leaves average 57.3. The range is what a canopy can do

vcmax25.prior_source: EEO: the coordination of the Rubisco- and light-limited rates at the site's growing-season daytime climate, with MEDS's own leaf (priors.py; Wang et al. 2017, Smith et al. 2019)

stomatal_g1.prior_source: EEO: the least-cost optimum at the site's growing-season daytime climate (priors.py; Prentice et al. 2014, Stocker et al. 2020, beta 146)

stomatal_g0.prior_source: the PFT file's value, a factor e either way: the residual conductance is poorly known

z0m_ratio.prior_source: the base value (ED2 0.13), +-0.04: closed canopies give z0/h of about 0.06-0.15 (Raupach 1994). Effective: it carries the canopy-air scheme's errors

wstress_sref_stomata.prior_source: the PFT file's value, a factor 2 either way (Sabot et al. 2022 fit 0.5-5 across species)

kappa.prior_source: best-practice plan §3.3: the tower's respiration is about the soil chambers' alone; the provider's note on the above-ground share (40-50 %)

meta.source: Lin et al. 2015 (Nature Climate Change 5, 459-464, Fig. 2e): tropical rainforest trees, 167 species

le.reason: the ratio is flat: no filter

h.reason: still rising at the top u* classes: no filter (the observation model's job)

closure.reason: H/Rnet rises with u* (+54%), LE/Rnet does not (-4%): the gap is H's

validation.rule: the calibrated cost below the default's, and no target's RMSE more than 10% worse
